summary: Diagnose the parked ping-pong reversed-item playlist blackout and produce a ranked, verified fix plan

plan.root_cause_verdict: TWO-LAYER VERDICT. Layer 1 — CONFIRMED (code-verified, ~certain): the shared gapless player has ZERO error handling — MasterPlaybackEngine.java's only listener is onMediaItemTransition (:182-209), the player is a stock ExoPlayer.Builder().build() (:288, no RenderersFactory, no decoder fallback), and the only onPlayerError in the faditor tree is log-only (FaditorPlayerManager.java:137). Any single-item failure therefore leaves the one player in a permanent error state = "black spread across every clip". This is the amplifier and the hard un-park blocker regardless of trigger. Layer 2 — the TRIGGER, ~65% confidence: the fwd→rev seam's HEVC(hvc1, device-probed on the actual remuxed playlist files)→AVC(avc1 libx264 bake) codec-family swap on the single player/surface — the ONLY structural delta vs the device-proven all-HEVC gapless case, MIME change makes codec reuse structurally impossible (MediaCodecInfo.canReuseCodec DISCARD_REASON_MIME_TYPE_CHANGED), and this exact swap is a documented black-screen/err-22 class on Samsung devices INCLUDING Qualcomm variants (ExoPlayer #8696, media #2185, #6454); media3 1.8.0's sleep-and-retry only covers the creation-throw variant, not silent black. Remaining ~35%: the baked AVC stream itself renders black on this device (host repro with the app's exact args: ~40 Mbps, 5x over its own declared H.264 L4.0 cap, plus the 90kHz-VFR source collapsing to 25fps; findroid #701 documents Note-9-family rendering out-of-capability AVC as silent black with audio). JUDGE'S CORRECTIONS forcing this split verdict: (1) the "Transformer export decoded the same baked file fine" claim that both investigators used to falsify the stream hypothesis is UNSUPPORTED — commit 9d9539c's title says parity is "by construction", handoff.md records no on-device export of a baked reversed segment (owed items: user eyeball, reverse audio never heard), parking came ~2h after L2 landed — so the stream hypothesis was never falsified; (2) this SM-N960U is SNAPDRAGON (sdm845, OMX.qcom decoders per vendor XML + media.metrics) — every Exynos-specific mechanism cited by external research is void; (3) AAR binary inspection (this session): libx264 + h264/hevc_mediacodec strings PRESENT in libavcodec.so, libx265/kvazaar/openh264 ABSENT — software-HEVC bake does not exist as a fallback. Instance exhaustion is ruled out (16+16 concurrent instances; KineMaster decodes AVC fine on this device). No logs from the blackout window survive, so the 65/35 split cannot be settled post-hoc — but the fix stack below eliminates BOTH triggers and contains any residual one, so the ambiguity does not block implementation; rank-1's instrumentation settles the verdict retroactively on first repro.

ranked_fixes.fix: Preview resilience + instrumentation (the ffcdc86 un-park prereq, correct under EVERY hypothesis). (a) Add onPlayerError to MasterPlaybackEngine's internalListener: capture PlaybackException.errorCode + player.getCurrentMediaItemIndex(), map via windows list to the failing WindowInfo; if it is a reverse rep, add that clip's reversed URI to a per-session poisoned set in the SourceResolver (resolveReversed returns null for poisoned entries), rebuild the playlist — that clip's reverse legs degrade to forward reps PER-CLIP (same math as the parked degrade, scoped) — and reseek to the pre-error visual position via the existing visualCursor bookkeeping, then resume. (b) Attach androidx.media3.exoplayer.util.EventLogger (debug-flag-gated) to the gapless player so onVideoInputFormatChanged / videoDecoderInitialized / videoDisabled / droppedFrames / onPlayerError are all in logcat — this recovers the error signature that no longer exists anywhere. (c) Fix un-park prereq #2, the rebuild race: add a monotonically increasing rebuildGeneration in FaditorEditorActivity; kickReverseBakeIfNeeded captures the generation at kick time and the bake-complete auto-promote rebuild is DISCARDED if the generation advanced (any user-initiated rebuild) since. (d) Flip Clip.PING_PONG_PARKED=false only after (a)-(c) land.
ranked_fixes.why: Certain, code-verified defect: with no error handling, ANY reversed-item failure permanently blacks the whole timeline — this is what turned a one-item decode problem into a feature-killing blackout, and ffcdc86's own body names it as un-park prereq. It also makes every subsequent experiment safe (worst case = one clip silently degrades forward) and its instrumentation is the ONLY remaining way to recover the real error code, since logcat/media.metrics/dropbox from the blackout window are all gone.

ranked_fixes.fix: Eliminate the codec switch: bake reversed segments as HEVC so the playlist stays hvc1 end-to-end, keeping ONE cache file for preview+export. In ReversedSegmentCache.bake(): attempt-1 command = `-ss .. -to .. -i IN -vf reverse,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS -af areverse,asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS -c:v hevc_mediacodec -pix_fmt nv12 -b:v 10M -g 30 -tag:v hvc1 -c:a aac -b:a 192k -movflags +faststart -y OUT` (mediacodec encoder needs explicit -b:v and yuv420p/nv12 input; do NOT pass -profile/-level — that is the suspected 0xffffffc3 trigger in the AVC sibling per scrcpy #5194 correlation); check FFmpegKit ReturnCode — attempt-2 on failure = same with `-pix_fmt yuv420p`; attempt-3 = the HARDENED libx264 command from rank 3. Record the winning codec in the cache filename/hash so stale artifacts can never be mistaken (bump the existing key hash — device cache is already empty). hevc_mediacodec is binary-confirmed present in the bundled AAR (this session); its reliability on this device is UNPROVEN and its AVC sibling failed configure with 0xffffffc3, hence the mandatory in-code chain — never ship the HEVC attempt without it.
ranked_fixes.why: Highest-leverage: a single-codec playlist removes the ONLY structural delta vs the device-proven all-HEVC gapless case, killing trigger-1 (codec-swap/surface race — reuse becomes possible, no decoder teardown at seams) AND trigger-2 (no AVC stream to be out-of-capability) simultaneously, while preserving the parity-by-construction invariant (export reads the same file; Transformer already decodes these HEVC sources). Verified this session that no software-HEVC encoder exists in the AAR, so hevc_mediacodec IS the HEVC path — the fallback chain makes its unproven reliability acceptable.

If HEVC bake fails on-device AND hardened AVC still blacks the seam, escalate to rank 4; the long-term heavy option is an in-app MediaCodec Surface-input reverse bake reusing the proven GLRecordingPipeline encoder stack (large, only if all cheap paths fail).

ranked_fixes.fix: Harden the libx264 bake (this is BOTH the rank-2 fallback leg and a standalone fix if rank 2 is skipped): replace the command tail with `-c:v libx264 -preset veryfast -crf 23 -profile:v high -level 4.0 -maxrate 12M -bufsize 24M -pix_fmt yuv420p -g 30 -fps_mode passthrough -c:a aac -b:a 192k -movflags +faststart`. This fixes three measured defects of the current command: (1) ~40 Mbps output overrunning the stream's own declared H.264 L4.0 (host repro, 5x over); (2) the 90kHz-timescale VFR source collapsing to ffmpeg's 25fps default with dropped frames (host repro: 52 packets from a ~60-frame cut) — -fps_mode passthrough preserves source timestamps (if the bundled ffmpeg 6.0 rejects -fps_mode, use `-vsync passthrough`, its 6.0-era alias); (3) unpinned profile. Also clamp the reverse-rep ClippingConfiguration endMs (MasterPlaybackEngine.java:373-375) to the baked file's ACTUAL probed duration rather than assuming it equals outPoint-inPoint, since a retimed bake can come up short.
ranked_fixes.why: Cheap, evidence-backed hardening: the bitrate/level overrun and VFR collapse were directly measured on a faithful host repro, and the Note 9 family is documented (findroid #701) to render out-of-capability AVC as silent black — exactly the unfalsified trigger-2. Even if trigger-1 is the real killer, this leg ships inside rank 2's fallback chain, so the effort is never wasted.

ranked_fixes.fix: Player-side codec-swap mitigations in the PREVIEW engine only (apply only if a mixed-codec playlist must survive, i.e. rank 2 failed): build the gapless player with `new ExoPlayer.Builder(context, new DefaultRenderersFactory(context).setEnableDecoderFallback(true))`; if the blackout persists, add a custom MediaCodecSelector (wrapping MediaCodecSelector.DEFAULT) that reorders getDecoderInfos to put c2.android.avc.decoder first for video/avc — software decode is viable for ≤30s 1080x1920 reversed reps and sidesteps the HW surface-handoff entirely. JUDGE'S NOTE — explicitly DOWNGRADED from the external report: do NOT bother overriding codecNeedsSetOutputSurfaceWorkaround; that path only fires on app-initiated setOutputSurface calls, not playlist codec swaps where the new codec configure()s with the surface at init.
ranked_fixes.why: Directly maintainer-recommended for decoder-switch init failures (ExoPlayer #3039, media #1460) and self-contained to MasterPlaybackEngine's builder line — but it treats the symptom, keeps a mixed-codec playlist, and setEnableDecoderFallback only helps when initialization THROWS (useless against a silent black render), so it ranks below eliminating the switch.
ranked_fixes.fallback_if_fails: If software AVC decode still blacks or stutters at seams, the shared-playlist approach for mixed codecs is exhausted — go to rank 5 or accept per-clip forward degrade (rank 1's behavior) as the shipped ping-pong experience on this device tier.

ranked_fixes.fix: LAST RESORT — second pre-warmed ExoPlayer dedicated to reversed items, swapped onto the PlayerView at each fwd↔rev seam. Decoder budget is NOT the objection (16+16 instances confirmed). Only implement if ranks 2-4 all demonstrably fail with logged evidence, and then prefer TWO stacked TextureViews (each player keeps its OWN surface, crossfade/alpha-swap at seams) over surface re-parenting, to avoid the handoff race.

Delete the corrupt file afterward so the cache re-bakes clean.

Only after ALL steps pass may PING_PONG_PARKED stay false in a commit.
risks: hevc_mediacodec may fail configure exactly like its AVC sibling (0xffffffc3) — it is binary-present but device-unproven, ffmpeg's docs call mediacodec encoding 'device dependent', and ffmpeg-kit is archived (no upstream fix will ever come). Mitigation is structural: never ship the HEVC attempt without the in-code fallback chain to hardened libx264.

Changing the baked file's codec changes shared-cache contents: the cache key/hash MUST be bumped or codec-tagged, or a device with a stale H.264 rev-*.mp4 could mix old/new bakes across preview and export and silently break parity (target device's cache is empty today; user devices may not be).

The 'Transformer export decoded the baked file fine' premise is folklore — do NOT let the implementation agent skip the export parity re-check on that basis; if Transformer unexpectedly chokes on the HEVC bake, fall back to the hardened-AVC bake as the shared file (export of AVC segments is then genuinely exercised for the first time).

Rank-1's on-error rebuild must reseek precisely and must not re-fire seam callbacks mid-rebuild, or it will regress the L1 seam-suppression behavior (caption/overlay rebind storms) that is currently device-proven; the regression-gate step exists specifically for this.

-fps_mode may not exist in the bundled ffmpeg 6.0 CLI parser (it landed around 5.1 but ffmpeg-kit builds vary) — if the bake errors on the flag, substitute -vsync passthrough; conversely the host-observed 25fps collapse itself is unconfirmed for the bundled build (host was 7.0.2), so probe the FIRST real device artifact before assuming the retime hazard was live.
screenrecord has produced 0-byte files on this device before — frame evidence collection may need multiple short recordings; do not accept 'looked fine by eye' as the only blackout-gone evidence.

Root-cause ambiguity is contained, not resolved: if rank 2 lands cleanly on the first try, the 65/35 trigger question stays formally open (both triggers die together). Acceptable — but keep the EventLogger flag available so any future field report of a black seam is immediately diagnosable.

All work touches FaditorEditorActivity/MasterPlaybackEngine god-files that other queued tracks (gesture contract, rebrand) also edit — per handoff.md coordination rules, only ONE agent on these files at a time; check git status before starting.

findings.summary: Blackout forensics complete. The parking commit ffcdc86 (2026-07-02 20:22) recorded the root cause only as "shared-player reversed-item decode failure" and documented the un-park prereq as "per-item decode fallback + rebuild race fix". Code reading shows: (a) the gapless engine is ONE ExoPlayer holding every clip and loop rep as playlist windows with native next-item pre-buffering, and it has NO onPlayerError handling anywhere — any single item that fails to decode takes down the whole player, which matches "black spread across every clip"; (b) reversed items are plain MediaItems (setUri + ClippingConfiguration, no format hints) pointing at a baked file that differs from its forward neighbors in exactly ONE structural dimension: video codec. Device byte-probes confirm the sandbox sources AND their remuxed playlist copies are HEVC Main L5.0 1080x1920 (hvc1/hvcC), while the bake forces libx264 ultrafast → H.264 Constrained Baseline (not High — the ultrafast preset disables the High-profile features) yuv420p GOP30 AAC MP4+faststart. So every fwd→rev seam demands a mid-playlist HEVC→AVC decoder swap on the shared player's one output surface — the prime suspect, since export (Transformer, fresh decoder, no mid-stream swap) handled the same file fine. The "bake as HEVC via hevc_mediacodec" premise is only half-validated: the Note 9 demonstrably HW-encodes HEVC 1080x1920 in-app, but via MediaCodec SURFACE input; ffmpeg-kit's mediacodec encoders use the byte-buffer path, and the sibling h264_mediacodec already failed on this exact device (Error 0xffffffc3), so hevc_mediacodec is unproven and could fail identically.

findings.summary: External research strongly supports the working theory that the ping-pong blackout is a known ExoPlayer/Android failure class: when adjacent playlist items change video MIME type (HEVC -> AVC), ExoPlayer MUST tear down the decoder and re-create a new one on the SAME output surface (codec reuse is impossible across MIME changes), and on Samsung/Exynos and other devices this codec-swap-on-one-surface step is a documented source of black screens and 'Failed to connect to surface, err -22' failures (google/ExoPlayer #8696, androidx/media #2185, google/ExoPlayer #6454). ExoPlayer's only shipped generic mitigation is a sleep-and-retry on MediaCodec creation (in since 2.17.0, so already inside FadCam's media3 1.8.0), which fixes the crash variant but not necessarily silent black output. Documented app-side mitigations: DefaultRenderersFactory.setEnableDecoderFallback(true), a custom MediaCodecSelector that forces the software AVC decoder for the baked items, and overriding MediaCodecVideoRenderer.codecNeedsSetOutputSurfaceWorkaround to force release+re-init (Note 9 is NOT in the built-in workaround device list). A second credible cause is the baked AVC stream itself: findroid #701 contains a Samsung Galaxy Note 9 / Android 10 report where an out-of-capability (10-bit) H.264 file plays BLACK with normal audio, i.e. this exact device family renders unsupported AVC as silent black video - so the libx264 output's profile/pix_fmt must be ffprobe'd and pinned. On the encoder side: MediaCodec ENCODING (hevc_mediacodec) only exists since FFmpeg 6.0, which FadCam's bundled ffmpeg-kit-full-6.0-2.LTS includes; FFmpeg docs call mediacodec encoding 'device dependent', input must be yuv420p/nv12, and the observed 0xffffffc3 configure failure matches an unresolved ffmpeg-kit issue (#1027, same 1080x1920 portrait + h264_mediacodec signature, closed not-planned, repo archived) and scrcpy reports where 0xffffffc3 is thrown when an unsupported profile/level is requested at configure(). Baking to HEVC via hevc_mediacodec to keep the playlist single-codec is therefore plausible-but-unproven (no Exynos-9810-specific encode reports found either way); the safest researched alternatives are (a) keep libx264 but pin -pix_fmt yuv420p and a conservative profile/level, plus force software AVC decode in preview only for baked items, or (b) eliminate the codec switch entirely.
facts: Codec reuse across playlist items is structurally impossible when the video MIME type changes: androidx/media MediaCodecInfo.canReuseCodec() sets DISCARD_REASON_MIME_TYPE_CHANGED (REUSE_RESULT_NO) whenever sampleMimeType differs, so an HEVC->AVC item boundary always releases the old MediaCodec and configures a brand-new one on the same surface — https://github.com/androidx/media/blob/release/libraries/exoplayer/src/main/java/androidx/media3/exoplayer/mediacodec/MediaCodecInfo.java (canReuseCodec, ~line 449; verified by downloading the raw file)

MediaCodec encoder' plus 'MediaCodec decoder via NDKMediaCodec') — verified in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/master/Changelog ; FadCam bundles ffmpeg-kit-full-6.0-2.LTS (C:\+Projects\Screenrecorder\FadCam\app\build.gradle.kts line 328), which is the FFmpeg 6.0 series, so hevc_mediacodec encode should exist in the bundled build

FFmpeg's official docs for the MediaCodec encoder wrapper state HEVC/H.264/VP8/VP9/AV1 encoding is supported but 'whether works or not is device dependent'; supported raw input pixel formats are yuv420p and nv12 (plus surface input); key options are ndk_codec, ndk_async, codec_name (pick a specific encoder implementation by name), bitrate_mode (cq/vbr/cbr/cbr_fd), pts_as_dts, operating_rate, qp_{i,p,b}_{min,max} — https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-codecs.html (verified from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/master/doc/encoders.texi §MediaCodec; pixel format map also verified in https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/blob/master/libavcodec/mediacodecenc.c)

The FadCam-observed h264_mediacodec failure is a known, UNRESOLVED ffmpeg-kit pattern: arthenica/ffmpeg-kit #1027 reports the identical signature (scale to 1080x1920 portrait, -c:v h264_mediacodec -b:v 7M -> 'Error 0xffffffc3' / 'MediaCodec configure failed, Generic error in an external library'); the reporter found libopenh264 worked; the issue was closed 'not planned' and the ffmpeg-kit repository is archived (no further updates) — https://github.com/arthenica/ffmpeg-kit/issues/1027

0xffffffc3 is observed to be thrown at MediaCodec.configure() when an unsupported encoder profile/level is requested: in scrcpy #5194 forcing AVCProfileHigh444+AVCLevel62 on OMX.qcom.video.encoder.avc produced Error 0xffffffc3 at every attempted resolution (1920 down to 800); scrcpy #3079 shows the same CodecException during ScreenEncoder.configure() with no official decode of the constant — https://github.com/Genymobile/scrcpy/issues/5194 and https://github.com/Genymobile/scrcpy/issues/3079

Documented app-side workarounds for decoder-switch failures, from ExoPlayer maintainers/issues: (a) DefaultRenderersFactory.setEnableDecoderFallback(true) to fall back to lower-priority (software) decoders when initialization fails, and (b) a custom MediaCodecSelector wrapping MediaCodecSelector.DEFAULT that reorders getDecoderInfos() to put the software H.264 decoder first for specific formats — https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/issues/3039 and https://github.com/androidx/media/issues/1460

MediaCodecVideoRenderer source acknowledges codec discard at non-adaptive transitions (e.g. playlist transitions) can visibly glitch: 'Many secure codecs introduce a black frame when discarded' (comment referencing https://github.com/androidx/media/issues/3120) — MediaCodecVideoRenderer.java shouldDiscardCodecForFrameRateChange (~line 2894, verified by download)

A related playlist-transition decode-init bug exists in current media3: androidx/media #2171 'Video Fails to Play When Last Media Item in Playlist' — a video item following items of a different codec type (images) throws a decoder initialization error depending on its position in the playlist — https://github.com/androidx/media/issues/2171

hypotheses.cause: Surface-handoff/codec-swap failure at the playlist seam: because MIME changes (HEVC->AVC), ExoPlayer releases OMX.Exynos.hevc.dec and configures a new AVC decoder on the same output surface; on Samsung/Exynos firmware the old codec's BufferQueue disconnect races the new codec's connect, yielding black output or err -22 (the #8696/#2185/#6454 failure class).
hypotheses.evidence_for: Exact symptom match (black at/around the reversed AVC item on a shared player); Samsung Exynos Android 10/11 devices repeatedly implicated (#8696); HEVC->AVC switch specifically reproduced as black screen in androidx/media #2185; export via Transformer (different surface lifecycle) handles the same file fine; Note 9 is NOT covered by ExoPlayer's built-in setOutputSurface workaround list, and the built-in Exynos adaptation workaround is gated to SDK<=25 secure decoders.
hypotheses.evidence_against: media3 1.8.0 already contains the sleep-and-retry MediaCodec-creation fix from 2.17.0, which should convert the race into a recovered init; most documented cases involve SECURE decoders or DRM transitions, while FadCam's content is clear; if configure failed outright ExoPlayer usually raises a player error rather than silently blacking out (whether an error was raised on the Note 9 is not recorded in the docs I read).
hypotheses.fix_sketch: In the preview engine only: attach an AnalyticsListener and log onVideoInputFormatChanged (with DecoderReuseEvaluation) + onVideoDecoderInitialized + onPlayerError around the seam to classify the failure; then try, in order: (1) custom MediaCodecSelector that forces c2.android.avc.decoder (software) for the baked AVC items, (2) DefaultRenderersFactory.setEnableDecoderFallback(true), (3) subclass MediaCodecVideoRenderer overriding codecNeedsSetOutputSurfaceWorkaround to return true (forces release+re-init instead of setOutputSurface).

hypotheses.cause: The baked libx264 stream itself is outside (or mishandled by) the Note 9 AVC hardware decoder's comfort zone (profile/pix_fmt/level not pinned in the bake command — e.g. High 4:4:4 or 10-bit output if the filter chain changes pix_fmt), and on this exact device family unsupported AVC renders as silent black video with audio still playing.
hypotheses.evidence_for: findroid #701 contains a Galaxy Note 9 / Android 10 report of 10-bit H.264 playing black-with-audio (even with software decode in mpv) and flickering in ExoPlayer — proving the 'silent black instead of error' behavior for out-of-capability AVC on this device; scrcpy #5194 shows codecs hard-reject exotic AVC profiles; libx264 picks profile/pix_fmt from input if not pinned.
hypotheses.evidence_against: Media3 Transformer exported the SAME baked file correctly with parity proven before parking, which strongly suggests the file is decodable by the device's AVC decoder (Transformer also uses MediaCodec decode on-device); phone recordings are almost certainly 8-bit HEVC so libx264 would default to yuv420p High, which the Note 9 supports.
hypotheses.fix_sketch: ffprobe the cached reversed segment (profile, pix_fmt, level, color range) from ReversedSegmentCache output; pin '-pix_fmt yuv420p -profile:v high -level 4.0' (or baseline/main as a test) in the bake command; A/B a re-baked clip in preview. If Transformer export really decoded the same file on-device, this hypothesis is largely falsified and H1 stands.

hypotheses.cause: Eliminating the codec switch is the highest-leverage fix: bake the reversed segment as HEVC so the playlist stays single-codec end-to-end — either via hevc_mediacodec hardware encode (present in the bundled FFmpeg 6.0) or another HEVC path.
hypotheses.evidence_for: Every documented failure mode found (codec reuse impossible across MIME, err -22 surface handoff, HEVC<->AVC switch issues #2185/#9250/#1542) disappears if adjacent items share video/hevc; hevc_mediacodec encoder exists in FFmpeg 6.0 / ffmpeg-kit 6.0 with documented options (set -b:v explicitly, input yuv420p/nv12, optional codec_name to pick OMX.Exynos.HEVC.Encoder, bitrate_mode).
hypotheses.evidence_against: FFmpeg docs explicitly say mediacodec encoding success is 'device dependent'; the sibling h264_mediacodec already failed with 0xffffffc3 on this device (though that may be a profile/level negotiation issue specific to the AVC wrapper path, not proof HEVC fails); zero public reports found for hevc_mediacodec encode on Exynos 9810 either way; ffmpeg-kit is archived so no upstream fixes will come.
hypotheses.fix_sketch: Device-experiment (outside my scope): run the existing bake command with '-c:v hevc_mediacodec -b:v <src bitrate> -pix_fmt nv12' (and if it 0xffffffc3s, retry with explicit '-codec_name OMX.Exynos.HEVC.Encoder' or c2.android.hevc.encoder, and without profile/level overrides); verify output plays in the preview playlist. Fallback single-codec option: transcode the FORWARD copies of looped clips to AVC too, so the seam is AVC->AVC (ugly but codec-switch-free).

hypotheses.cause: Exynos decoder instance/resource exhaustion: the preview session (or other app components — thumbnails, camera, a second prepared player) holds enough codec instances that the new AVC decoder allocation at the seam fails, which presents as black video on OMX.Exynos devices.
hypotheses.evidence_for: OMX.Exynos.avc.dec init failures with black player view are documented under multi-instance/resource pressure (google/ExoPlayer #9230, #5799); a codec-switch seam is exactly where a new instance must be allocated while the old one may not yet be released.
hypotheses.evidence_against: A single MasterPlaybackEngine playlist normally holds one video codec at a time (old is released before new init when reuse is impossible); the blackout reproduces deterministically at the reversed item rather than sporadically under load, which fits H1/H2 better.
hypotheses.fix_sketch: During the seam, dump 'adb shell dumpsys media.player'/mediametrics or log MediaCodecInfo.getMaxSupportedInstances; ensure no other ExoPlayer/MediaMetadataRetriever/thumbnail codecs are alive during preview; if implicated, pre-release ancillary codec users before playback.

open_questions: Authoritative meaning of MediaCodec error 0xffffffc3: no official decode of the constant was found anywhere; the 'unsupported profile/level at configure()' interpretation rests on correlation in scrcpy #5194/#3079 and ffmpeg-kit #1027, not on AOSP documentation.

Whether androidx/media #2185 (HEVC<->AVC switch black screen on Android 11) was ever actually fixed in a media3 release — the thread shows the reporter claiming ExoPlayer 2.14.1 had a 50 ms retry workaround, while the release notes I verified place the 'sleep and retry' fix in 2.17.0; the black-screen (non-crashing) variant may remain unfixed in 1.8.0.

No public evidence found either way on hevc_mediacodec ENCODING reliability on Exynos 9810 / Note 9 specifically (searches returned only decode-side reports like mpv-android #170); only a device experiment can answer this.

Whether the Note 9 preview blackout is accompanied by a Player error / DecoderInitializationException in logcat or is a truly silent black render — this determines whether it is the init-failure variant (retryable, decoder-fallback helps) or the silent-surface variant (needs software decode or codec-switch elimination); requires the device-side investigator.

Actual profile/pix_fmt/level/color-range of the baked reversed file (ffprobe of the ReversedSegmentCache output) — needed to confirm or eliminate the 'stream outside decoder capability' hypothesis (H2), especially since Transformer export parity argues against it.

Whether ffmpeg-kit-full-6.0-2.LTS's libx264 is built 8-bit-only (near-certain but unverified); if 10-bit-capable, a 10-bit source could silently produce Hi10P output, which findroid #701 shows renders black on the Note 9.

Whether the 'sleep and retry' fix applies to the FadCam failure at all: it triggers only when MediaCodec CREATION throws; if the Exynos decoder initializes successfully but renders black frames onto the reused surface, no shipped ExoPlayer workaround covers it (the setOutputSurface workaround list explicitly excludes this device and only fires on app-initiated surface changes, not playlist codec swaps).
